newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday March 4.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Italian military helicopters swooped into Albania to evacuate 35 people trapped in the riot-torn southern port of Vlore amid fears that the small Balkan state was on the verge of war (all).

* Parliamentary leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) Fabio Mussi said that the government was entering a difficult period and criticised the position of hard-left Communist Refoundation party, adding that relations between the members of the majority coalition were "not sailing in calm waters". Mussi told reporters that the government was "facing the usual problems, always on the knife edge, with Refoundation always threatening to withdraw support" (all).

* In an interview with Spanish newspaper "El Pais", Prime Minister Romano Prodi was quoted as saying the hard left Communist Refoumdation party was a brake for the government, and the government could have done more without it (all).

* Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said that Italian public sector borrowing requirement over the first two months of the year was in line with government targets, yet a fresh mini-budget will still be needed (all).
* Italy's PSBR in March is said to approach 15 trillion lire according to preliminary estimates (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco launched a plan to fight tax evasion in Italy, targetting companies with sales of over 50 billion lire (all).

* Italy's industrialists' association Confindustria's president Giorgio Fossa said that, taking into account the low rate of inflation, it would now be necessary to revise the labour agreement of July 1993. Unions' leader Sergio Cofferati replied that the treaty should instead be strengthened and thoroughly applied (all).
* In an interview, Yves-Thibault de Silguy, EU Commissioner for monetary affairs, said there will be no postponement of EMU, otherwise as it would endanger the whole project (La Stampa).

* Financial holding Gemina SpA said it formally signed the contract spinning off its industrial activities setting up a holding company called HPI. A statement said a nine-member board had been named for HPI, with Nicolo Nefri appointed as chairman (all).
* New Holland, in which Fiat has a 69 percent stake, said its 1996 net income rose to $250 million after $221 million in 1995. Revenues rose to $5.547 billion from $5 billion in 1995 (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
